description: Peak-since-boot hwmon sensor high-water marks, zone-resolved ACPI thermal zones, and true energy integrated from the DCGM energy counter. All three datasets come straight off the 1,898 GB300 trays. Live sensor readings and module power meters are owned by the Tray Sensors & Module Meters board; GPU core/HBM temperature, GPU power draw and the DCGM violation counters are owned by GPU Health and GPU Error Surface, and are deliberately not duplicated here.

options.content: Thermal history and integrated energy. The three datasets on this board are the ones that are not instantaneous: the peak temperature each hwmon sensor has recorded since the tray booted, the 26 zone-resolved ACPI thermal zones per tray, and true energy in kWh integrated from the DCGM energy counter. Live sensor readings are on Tray Sensors & Module Meters; GPU core/HBM temperature and GPU power are on GPU Health.

panels.title: Peak sensor temperature since boot — the high-water mark each hwmon sensor holds

panels.description:
max(node_hwmon_temp_highest_celsius) over the selected SUs and racks. This is the hottest any tray sensor has been since that tray booted, not the temperature now.

L2: the table 'Peak-temperature leaders — top 50' below uses the same selector and the same $su/$rack filter; its first row IS this number.
panels.title: Highest peak recorded

panels.description:
count(count by(node)(node_hwmon_temp_highest_celsius >= 90)) — trays holding at least one sensor whose recorded peak reached 90 °C.

L2: the table 'Trays with a peak at or above 90 °C' below is the same selector and the same threshold, one row per tray; its row count IS this number.
panels.title: Trays with a peak at or above 90 °C

panels.description: topk(50, node_hwmon_temp_highest_celsius) with the hwmon chip class joined in. Same selector and same $su/$rack filter as the tile above, so the top row equals it exactly.
panels.title: Peak-temperature leaders — top 50 sensors · row 1 is the “Highest peak recorded” tile

panels.description: count by(node,rack,su)(node_hwmon_temp_highest_celsius >= 90) — same selector, same threshold and same $su/$rack filter as the tile above, one row per tray. The row count IS the tile.
panels.title: Trays with a peak at or above 90 °C — the exact trays (rows = the tile above)
ACPI thermal zones — zone-resolved, 26 zones on every tray

panels.description:
max(node_thermal_zone_temp) over the selected SUs and racks.

L2: the table 'Hottest ACPI zones — top 50' below uses the same selector and the same $su/$rack filter; its first row IS this number.
panels.title: Hottest ACPI zone now

panels.description:
count(node_thermal_zone_temp) — total ACPI thermal-zone readings in scope.

L2: the 'By zone index' table below is the same selector; its 'Zones' column sums to this number.
panels.title: Zones reporting

panels.description:
count(count by(zone)(node_thermal_zone_temp)) — how many distinct ACPI zone indices the trays expose.

L2: the 'By zone index' table below is the same selector grouped by zone; its row count IS this number.
panels.title: Distinct zone indices

panels.description: topk(50, node_thermal_zone_temp). Same selector and same $su/$rack filter as the tile above, so the top row equals it exactly.
panels.title: Hottest ACPI zones — top 50 · row 1 is the “Hottest ACPI zone now” tile

panels.description: count / max / avg by(zone) over node_thermal_zone_temp with the same selector and the same $su/$rack filter as the two tiles above.
panels.title: By zone index — one row per zone (rows = “Distinct zone indices”; the Zones column sums to “Zones reporting”)

panels.description: max and mean of node_thermal_zone_temp over the selected SUs and racks — two series, so this stays cheap at any scope.
panels.title: ACPI zone temperature across the estate
Energy — integrated from the DCGM energy counter over the selected window

panels.description:
sum(increase(DCGM_FI_DEV_TOTAL_ENERGY_CONSUMPTION[$__range])) / 3.6e9 — true energy from the counter, not an average-power estimate. Changes with the dashboard time range.

L2: the 'Energy by rack' table below uses the same expression and the same $su/$rack filter; its kWh column sums to this number.
panels.title: Energy consumed in window

panels.description:
count(count by(rack,su)(increase(DCGM_FI_DEV_TOTAL_ENERGY_CONSUMPTION[$__range]))) — deliberately built on increase() over the same window as the table below, not on an instant read, so the two cannot disagree.

L2: the 'Energy by rack' table below is the same expression; its row count IS this number.
panels.title: Racks reporting energy counters in window

panels.description:
max(sum by(rack,su)(increase(DCGM_FI_DEV_TOTAL_ENERGY_CONSUMPTION[$__range])) / 3.6e9).

L2: the 'Energy by rack' table below is the same expression; its first row IS this number.
panels.title: Busiest rack in window

panels.description: sum by(rack,su)(increase(DCGM_FI_DEV_TOTAL_ENERGY_CONSUMPTION[$__range])) / 3.6e9, plus mean draw over the same window and the GPU and tray counts on the same increase() basis. Every column uses the same expression, the same window and the same $su/$rack filter as the three tiles above. A full GB300 rack reads 18 trays and 72 GPUs.
panels.title: Energy by rack — one row per rack (rows = “Racks reporting energy counters in window”; kWh sums to the energy tile; row 1 is the busiest rack)
